headline: Learned representations adapt to cell imaging and single-cell omics under limited labels
label: Representation Learning For Cell Imaging
summary: Label scarcity and cross-modal heterogeneity are driving cell-level models toward self-supervised, semi-supervised, and quality-aware designs.
synthesis: The dominant thread is adapting learned representations to cell-level imaging and omics data under limited labels. Cell-DINO applies self-supervised DINOv2 vision transformers to fluorescence microscopy, yielding morphology embeddings that outperform supervised approaches. Fluoro-forest offers a semi-supervised random forest workflow for cell type annotation in cyclic immunofluorescence with limited training data. Contrastive learning with time-based augmentations improves cell division detection and tracking in live cell imaging. SpaceTrooper scores per-cell quality from expression and morphology rather than fixed thresholds. Other items address integration, imputation, and clustering in single-cell omics, a distinct strand. What is new is explicit reliance on limited training data and per-cell quality scoring rather than fixed settings.
